summary: Nobuhiro Ota is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo between roughly 1988 and 2001. He held positions at the University of Tokyo and later Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, becoming a professor there in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University. His career includes serving as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpńin, attested in 2014.

Nobumasa Hibi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Rissho University from around 1955 to 1959. He later served as an assistant professor at Rissho University, attested in 1972.

Tenshō Miyazaki is a scholar of Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who completed his doctorate at the University of Tokyo around 2010. He held research positions at Toyo University and the University of Tokyo.

Nobumi Iyanaga is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at École Pratique des Hautes Études (1968–1969). He held a research contract at École française d'Extrême-Orient (2008–2014) and lectured at the University of Tokyo.
Nobuo Otsuka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a researcher in 1995.

Nobuyoshi Yamabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Agriculture (2003) and Waseda University (appointed 2015).

Nobuyuki Kaji is a philosopher and sinologist educated at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. He served as professor at Osaka University (1984–1998), president of Koshien Junior College, and special invited professor at Ritsumeikan University (2008–2015).

Nobuyuki Watase is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a master's degree from Kyoto University around 1966. He served as an assistant professor at Tokai University (~1982–2007) and president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2011).
Nobuyuki Yamagiwa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and is attested as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Genjun Sasaki and Issai Funahashi. He held multiple academic posts at Otani University, including lecturer and departmental appointee.
Noel Salmond is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held academic posts at Bishop's University (attested 1995–1996) and Carleton University (attested 1997–2000).

Nolan Pliny Jacobson was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. He taught at several American colleges and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Winthrop University (1954–1974).

Noopur Shalini works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at IGNOU, Ningbo University, and the University of Mumbai, she was appointed to the Department of Archaeology at Zhejiang University in 2023.

Nora Kershaw Chadwick was a historian and linguist who studied at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1911–1914). She held posts at the University of St Andrews (~1919–1923) and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).

Norbert M. Samuelson was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. He served as professor at Temple University (1975–1998) and held an endowed chair at Arizona State University.

Noriaki Hakamaya is a Buddhist studies scholar, Tibetologist, and philosopher educated at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi and Shun'ei Hirai. He was a longtime professor at Komazawa University (1985–2011).

Noriaki Hosoda is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held positions as assistant and assistant professor at Hokkaido University and is attested as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.
Noriaki Inoue is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University from roughly 1949 to 1953. He later served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1982.

Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He spent his academic career at Bukkyo University, serving as professor from 1994 and professor emeritus from 2015 to 2021.
